title: add-tenant-streaming-log-sampler-token-budget-and-alert-fanout-gate
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We see recurring alert storms triggered by long-tail streaming invocations that generate large log volumes and drive high token-level cost spikes for certain tenants. Existing sampling is per-invocation and reactive; it doesn't respect tenant budgets and generates noisy fanout for routing alerts. This PR introduces a tenant-aware streaming log sampler plus a token-budget controller and an alert-fanout gate to (1) bound streaming log emission by tenant token budget, (2) provide graceful quiet windows for noisy tenants, and (3) throttle alert fanout to downstream notification channels to prevent escalation storms.

What this changes (high level):
- Streaming log sampler: continuous reservoir sampler that tracks per-invocation cost and sampling weight, implemented in services/observability/sampler.go. The sampler is adaptive to prompt-shape (prefix vs generated tokens) and respects per-tenant budget quotas.
- Token-budget controller: lightweight in-memory + persisted lease manager that keeps an escrow of token budget per tenant and exposes an API for sampler decisions (services/observability/budget_controller.go). Budgets are refilled on a sliding window and can be provisioned via Console.
- Alert-fanout gate: per-tenant rate-limiter for alert notifications that coalesces similar alerts and applies backpressure to downstream channels (pkg/alerting/fanout_gate.go). Gate is configurable with quiet windows and escalation thresholds.
- Dashboards and alerts: adds dashboards/dashboards/streaming_budget_overview.json and alerting/rules/streaming_budget_alerts.yaml to visualize sampler throughput, token escrow levels, and suppressed/forwarded alert counts.
- Runbook & examples: tools/runbooks/sampler-runbook.md and examples/observability/streaming-sampler-quickstart.md documenting behavior, operational knobs, and rollout instructions.

Design notes:
- Sampling decision is deterministic per-invocation by hashing invocation fingerprint + tenant id to ensure reproducible sampling for debugging.
- Budget controller uses a soft-lease model: sampler may temporarily overshoot by a configurable burst but triggers an enforcement cooldown that reduces sampling probability for subsequent invocations.
- Alert-fanout gate keeps a small sliding window of recent alerts (compact digest) and suppresses duplicates, emitting a single summary when thresholds are exceeded. Backpressure is applied to the Notification Broker rather than the caller path to avoid user-visible errors.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy sampler and budget controller in opt-in mode behind a feature flag (default off).
2) Enable for a single low-traffic tenant and monitor dashboards for sampling ratio, escrow usage, and suppressed alerts.
3) Gradual ramp (2x tenants/day) with automated rollback if suppressed_alert_rate > 5% and user-visible latency or error increases.
4) Flip flag org-wide after 2 weeks and confirm steady-state.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of sampler + budget controller + gate
- [x] Unit & integration tests (tests/observability/sampler_test.go)
- [x] Dashboard and alerting rules
- [x] Runbook + quickstart docs
- [x] Feature flag gating and console integration

Related: ENG-9301 (observability backlog), ENG-9445 (alert fatigue initiative). See runbook link: docs/runbooks/observability/streaming-sampler (internal).

Notes: CI initially failed on a race in budget_controller when running high-concurrency test; fixed by switching to a per-tenant mutex striping strategy and adding a concurrency unit test. No API breaking changes. The feature is behind a flag; default is opt-out.

release_notes: Introduces a tenant-aware streaming log sampler that respects token budgets, a token-budget controller with soft-lease enforcement, and an alert-fanout gate to reduce escalation storms. Feature is behind a feature flag (observability.streaming_sampler). Adds dashboards and runbook. No breaking changes.
